goal: Extract the responsibility for managing enforced attributes from Safelist into a dedicated class (SafelistEnforcedAttributes). Move the enforcedAttributes storage and the public methods that manipulate enforced attributes (addEnforcedAttribute, removeEnforcedAttribute, getEnforcedAttributes) into the new class, and update Safelist internals to delegate to the new class. Update internal call sites in Safelist (factory methods, safety checks, copy ctor) so behavior is preserved.

expected_impact.rationale: Three public Safelist methods related to enforced-attribute management (addEnforcedAttribute, removeEnforcedAttribute, getEnforcedAttributes) are moved into a new class SafelistEnforcedAttributes and removed from Safelist; this reduces Safelist's public method count by 3 and reduces total method count and class LOC. Supporting references in Safelist (isSafeAttribute, shouldAbsUrl, and the copy constructor) are updated to call the new class' API, preserving behavior.

ops.details: Create a new package-visible class org.jsoup.safety.SafelistEnforcedAttributes that encapsulates Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, AttributeValue>> enforcedAttributes and provides instance methods: addEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute, String value), removeEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute), getEnforcedAttributes(String tagName) returning org.jsoup.nodes.Attributes, and internal helpers getEnforcedValue(Safelist.TagName tag, Safelist.AttributeKey key) and hasEnforcedAttribute(Safelist.TagName tag, Safelist.AttributeKey key). The new class will have a constructor that accepts the owning Safelist (to add the tag to the owner's tagNames when adding enforced attributes) and a copy constructor for deep copy. The class is placed in the same package (org.jsoup.safety) and uses Safelist's nested types (TagName, AttributeKey, AttributeValue).

Remove the field 'private final Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, AttributeValue>> enforcedAttributes' from Safelist and place equivalent storage inside SafelistEnforcedAttributes (as a private field). Introduce in Safelist a new private final field 'SafelistEnforcedAttributes enforced' initialized in Safelist() and copied in Safelist(Safelist copy).

Move the following public Safelist methods into SafelistEnforcedAttributes and remove them from Safelist: addEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute, String value), removeEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute), getEnforcedAttributes(String tagName). Implement the same logic in the new class, preserving validation (Validate.notEmpty(...)) and behavior. Provide copy constructor support in SafelistEnforcedAttributes so Safelist(Safelist copy) can deep copy the enforced attributes map.

Update internal Safelist code to use the new SafelistEnforcedAttributes API: 1) In isSafeAttribute(...) replace direct enforcedAttributes map access with calls to enforced.getEnforcedValue(tag, key) (and compare values as before). 2) In shouldAbsUrl(...) replace checks against enforcedAttributes map with enforced.hasEnforcedAttribute(tag, key) so behavior (returning false if enforced attribute present) is preserved. 3) In the Safelist copy constructor, deep-copy the enforced attributes by constructing new SafelistEnforcedAttributes(copy.enforced). 4) Update factory builder methods (e.g., basic()) which previously chained .addEnforcedAttribute(...) to instead call the new manager via the created Safelist instance, e.g.: Safelist s = new Safelist(); ...; s.enforced.addEnforcedAttribute("a","rel","nofollow"); return s; This removes the chained call and preserves behavior. All modifications remain within the two files in this block.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
